title: Human-Centric Lighting in Classroom Design: Effects on Student Cognition and Performance – A Systematic Review

findings.antecedent: Human-Centric Lighting (HCL) systems (simulating natural day and night cycles, properly dosed light exposure, higher illumination and color temperatures)
findings.consequent: attention, working memory, information processing speed, executive functions, overall academic performance, concentration, cognitive abilities, mood, reading performance, ability to switch tasks, student efficiency
key_citations: Fisk, A. S., Tam, S. K. E., Brown, L. A., Vyazovskiy, V. V., Bannerman, D. M., & Peirson, S. N. (2018)
Kent, S. T., McClure, L. A., Crosson, W. L., Arnett, D. K., Wadley, V. G., & Sathiakumar, N. (2009)
Siraji, M. A., Kalavally, V., Schaefer, A., & Haque, S. (2022)
Y. -T. Yang, W. -C. Chiang and J. -S. Wang, (2023)
Sleegers, P., Moolenaar, N., Galetzka, M., Pruyn, A. T., Sarroukh, B., & Van Der Zande, B. (2012)
Mott MS, Robinson DH, Walden A, Burnette J, Rutherford AS. (2012)
findings.quote: Key findings indicate promising evidence that Human Centric Lighting (HCL) systems, simulating natural day and night cycles by adjusting lighting parameters, can improve attention, working memory, information processing speed, executive functions, and overall academic performance of students.

findings.antecedent: Human-Centric Lighting (HCL) systems (adapting classroom lighting to natural light cycles, lower illumination and color temperatures)
findings.consequent: feelings of fatigue, restlessness, disturbances in the classroom
key_citations: Sleegers, P., Moolenaar, N., Galetzka, M., Pruyn, A. T., Sarroukh, B., & Van Der Zande, B. (2012)
findings.quote: adapting classroom lighting to natural light cycles can enhance student learning and well-being... helps reduce feelings of fatigue and increase student efficiency.

findings.antecedent: Human-Centric Lighting (HCL) systems (simulating natural light patterns, high levels of blue light in the morning and warmer tones towards the evening)
findings.consequent: sleep quality, alertness, overall well-being, synchronization of circadian rhythms, cognitive functions, emotional states, subjective sleepiness
key_citations: Y. -T. Yang, W. -C. Chiang and J. -S. Wang, (2023)
findings.quote: HCL systems can simulate natural light patterns, aligning with the human circadian rhythm, which has been linked to improved sleep quality, alertness, and overall well-being.

findings.consequent: relaxing ambience, social interaction, efficiency of breaks and relaxation
findings.quote: During group exercises, slightly dimmed warm white light is used to create a relaxing ambience and support social interaction, enhancing the efficiency of breaks and relaxation.
